45	    if len(arr) < 2:
46	        return np.zeros(shape=x.shape, dtype=np.int32), np.zeros_like(x)
47	    index = np.clip(np.searchsorted(arr, x, side="right") - 1, 0, len(arr) - 2)
48	    # Use broadcasting to avoid repeated array access
49	    arr_index = arr[index]
50	    arr_next = arr[np.clip(index + 1, 1, len(arr) - 1)]  # Ensure we don't go out of bounds
51	    bcoord = (x - arr_index) / (arr_next - arr_index)
52	
53	    # TODO check how we can avoid searchsorted when grid spacing is uniform
54	    # dx = arr[1] - arr[0]
55	    # index = ((x - arr[0]) / dx).astype(int)
56	    # index = np.clip(index, 0, len(arr) - 2)
57	    # bcoord = (x - arr[index]) / dx
58	
59	    index = np.where(x < arr[0], LEFT_OUT_OF_BOUNDS, index)
60	    index = np.where(x > arr[-1], RIGHT_OUT_OF_BOUNDS, index)
61	
62	    return np.atleast_1d(index), np.atleast_1d(bcoord)

94	def curvilinear_point_in_cell(grid, y: np.ndarray, x: np.ndarray, yi: np.ndarray, xi: np.ndarray):
95	    xsi = eta = -1.0 * np.ones(len(x), dtype=float)
96	    invA = np.array(
97	        [
98	            [1, 0, 0, 0],
99	            [-1, 1, 0, 0],
100	            [-1, 0, 0, 1],
101	            [1, -1, 1, -1],
102	        ]
103	    )
104	
105	    px = np.array([grid.lon[yi, xi], grid.lon[yi, xi + 1], grid.lon[yi + 1, xi + 1], grid.lon[yi + 1, xi]])
106	
107	    if grid._mesh == "spherical":
108	        # Map grid and particle longitudes to [-180,180)
109	        px = ((px + 180.0) % 360.0) - 180.0
110	        x = ((x + 180.0) % 360.0) - 180.0
111	
112	        # Create a mask for antimeridian cells
113	        lon_span = px.max(axis=0) - px.min(axis=0)
114	        antimeridian_cell = lon_span > 180.0
115	
116	        if np.any(antimeridian_cell):
117	            # For any antimeridian cell ...
118	            #  If particle longitude is closer to 180.0, then negative cell longitudes need to be bumped by +360
119	            mask = (px < 0.0) & antimeridian_cell[np.newaxis, :] & (x[np.newaxis, :] > 0.0)
120	            px[mask] += 360.0
121	            #  If particle longitude is closer to -180.0, then positive cell longitudes need to be bumped by -360
122	            mask = (px > 0.0) & antimeridian_cell[np.newaxis, :] & (x[np.newaxis, :] < 0.0)
123	            px[mask] -= 360.0
124	
125	    py = np.array([grid.lat[yi, xi], grid.lat[yi, xi + 1], grid.lat[yi + 1, xi + 1], grid.lat[yi + 1, xi]])
126	
127	    a, b = np.dot(invA, px), np.dot(invA, py)
128	    aa = a[3] * b[2] - a[2] * b[3]
129	    bb = a[3] * b[0] - a[0] * b[3] + a[1] * b[2] - a[2] * b[1] + x * b[3] - y * a[3]
130	    cc = a[1] * b[0] - a[0] * b[1] + x * b[1] - y * a[1]
131	    det2 = bb * bb - 4 * aa * cc
132	
133	    with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
134	        det = np.where(det2 > 0, np.sqrt(det2), eta)
135	        eta = np.where(abs(aa) < 1e-12, -cc / bb, np.where(det2 > 0, (-bb + det) / (2 * aa), eta))
136	
137	        xsi = np.where(
138	            abs(a[1] + a[3] * eta) < 1e-12,
139	            ((y - py[0]) / (py[1] - py[0]) + (y - py[3]) / (py[2] - py[3])) * 0.5,
140	            (x - a[0] - a[2] * eta) / (a[1] + a[3] * eta),
141	        )
142	    is_in_cell = np.where((xsi >= 0) & (xsi <= 1) & (eta >= 0) & (eta <= 1), 1, 0)
143	
144	    return is_in_cell, np.column_stack((xsi, eta))

147	def _search_indices_curvilinear_2d(
148	    grid: XGrid, y: np.ndarray, x: np.ndarray, yi: np.ndarray | None = None, xi: np.ndarray | None = None
149	):
150	    """Searches a grid for particle locations in 2D curvilinear coordinates.
151	
152	    Parameters
153	    ----------
154	    grid : XGrid
155	        The curvilinear grid to search within.
156	    y : np.ndarray
157	        Array of latitude-coordinates of the points to locate.
158	    x : np.ndarray
159	        Array of longitude-coordinates of the points to locate.
160	    yi : np.ndarray | None, optional
161	        Array of initial guesses for the j indices of the points to locate.
162	    xi : np.ndarray | None, optional
163	        Array of initial guesses for the i indices of the points to locate.
164	
165	    Returns
166	    -------
167	    tuple
168	        A tuple containing four elements:
169	        - yi (np.ndarray): Array of found j-indices corresponding to the input coordinates.
170	        - eta (np.ndarray): Array of barycentric coordinates in the j-direction within the found grid cells.
171	        - xi (np.ndarray): Array of found i-indices corresponding to the input cooordinates.
172	        - xsi (np.ndarray): Array of barycentric coordinates in the i-direction within the found grid cells.
173	    """
174	    if np.any(xi):
175	        # If an initial guess is provided, we first perform a point in cell check for all guessed indices
176	        is_in_cell, coords = curvilinear_point_in_cell(grid, y, x, yi, xi)
177	        y_check = y[is_in_cell == 0]
178	        x_check = x[is_in_cell == 0]
179	        zero_indices = np.where(is_in_cell == 0)[0]
180	    else:
181	        # Otherwise, we need to check all points
182	        yi = np.full(len(y), GRID_SEARCH_ERROR, dtype=np.int32)
183	        xi = np.full(len(x), GRID_SEARCH_ERROR, dtype=np.int32)
184	        y_check = y
185	        x_check = x
186	        coords = -1.0 * np.ones((len(y), 2), dtype=np.float32)
187	        zero_indices = np.arange(len(y))
188	
189	    # If there are any points that were not found in the first step, we query the spatial hash for those points
190	    if len(zero_indices) > 0:
191	        yi_q, xi_q, coords_q = grid.get_spatial_hash().query(y_check, x_check)
192	        # Only those points that were not found in the first step are updated
193	        coords[zero_indices, :] = coords_q
194	        yi[zero_indices] = yi_q
195	        xi[zero_indices] = xi_q
196	
197	    xsi = coords[:, 0]
198	    eta = coords[:, 1]
199	
200	    return (yi, eta, xi, xsi)

203	def uxgrid_point_in_cell(grid, y: np.ndarray, x: np.ndarray, yi: np.ndarray, xi: np.ndarray):
204	    """Check if points are inside the grid cells defined by the given face indices.
205	
206	    Parameters
207	    ----------
208	    grid : ux.grid.Grid
209	        The uxarray grid object containing the unstructured grid data.
210	    y : np.ndarray
211	        Array of latitudes of the points to check.
212	    x : np.ndarray
213	        Array of longitudes of the points to check.
214	    yi : np.ndarray
215	        Not used, but included for compatibility with other search functions.
216	    xi : np.ndarray
217	        Array of face indices corresponding to the points.
218	
219	    Returns
220	    -------
221	    is_in_cell : np.ndarray
222	        An array indicating whether each point is inside (1) or outside (0) the corresponding cell.
223	    coords : np.ndarray
224	        Barycentric coordinates of the points within their respective cells.
225	    """
226	    if grid._mesh == "spherical":
227	        lon_rad = np.deg2rad(x)
228	        lat_rad = np.deg2rad(y)
229	        x_cart, y_cart, z_cart = _latlon_rad_to_xyz(lat_rad, lon_rad)
230	        points = np.column_stack((x_cart.flatten(), y_cart.flatten(), z_cart.flatten()))  # (M,3)
231	
232	        # Get the vertex indices for each face
233	        nids = grid.uxgrid.face_node_connectivity[xi].values
234	        face_vertices = np.stack(
235	            (
236	                grid.uxgrid.node_x[nids.ravel()].values.reshape(nids.shape),
237	                grid.uxgrid.node_y[nids.ravel()].values.reshape(nids.shape),
238	                grid.uxgrid.node_z[nids.ravel()].values.reshape(nids.shape),
239	            ),
240	            axis=-1,
241	        )
242	
243	        # Get projection points onto element plane. Keep the leading
244	        # dimension even for single-face queries so shapes remain (M,3).
245	        r1 = face_vertices[:, 1, :] - face_vertices[:, 0, :]
246	        r2 = face_vertices[:, 2, :] - face_vertices[:, 0, :]
247	        nhat = np.cross(r1, r2)
248	        norm = np.linalg.norm(nhat, axis=-1)
249	        # Avoid division by zero for degenerate faces
250	        norm = np.where(norm == 0.0, 1.0, norm)
251	        nhat = nhat / norm[:, None]
252	        # Calculate the component of the points in the direction of nhat
253	        ptilde = points - face_vertices[:, 0, :]
254	        pdotnhat = np.sum(ptilde * nhat, axis=-1)
255	        # Reconstruct points with normal component removed.
256	        points = ptilde - pdotnhat[:, None] * nhat + face_vertices[:, 0, :]
257	
258	    else:
259	        nids = grid.uxgrid.face_node_connectivity[xi, :].values
260	        face_vertices = np.stack(
261	            (
262	                grid.uxgrid.node_lon[nids.ravel()].values.reshape(nids.shape),
263	                grid.uxgrid.node_lat[nids.ravel()].values.reshape(nids.shape),
264	            ),
265	            axis=-1,
266	        )
267	        points = np.stack((x, y), axis=-1)
268	
269	    M = len(points)
270	
271	    coords = _barycentric_coordinates(face_vertices, points)
272	
273	    is_in_cell = np.zeros(M, dtype=np.int32)
274	    is_in_cell = np.where(np.all((coords >= -1e-6), axis=1), 1, 0)
275	    is_in_cell &= np.isclose(np.sum(coords, axis=1), 1.0, rtol=1e-3, atol=1e-6)
276	
277	    return is_in_cell, coords

280	def _triangle_area(A, B, C):  # noqa: N803
281	    """Compute the area of a triangle given by three points."""
282	    d1 = B - A
283	    d2 = C - A
284	    if A.shape[-1] == 2:
285	        # 2D case: cross product reduces to scalar z-component
286	        cross = d1[..., 0] * d2[..., 1] - d1[..., 1] * d2[..., 0]
287	        area = 0.5 * cross
288	    elif A.shape[-1] == 3:
289	        # 3D case: full vector cross product
290	        cross = np.cross(d1, d2)
291	        area = 0.5 * np.linalg.norm(cross, axis=-1)
292	    else:
293	        raise ValueError(f"Expected last dim=2 or 3, got {A.shape[-1]}")
294	
295	    return area

298	def _barycentric_coordinates(nodes, points, min_area=1e-8):
299	    """
300	    Compute the barycentric coordinates of a point P inside a convex polygon using area-based weights.
301	    This method currently only works for triangular cells (K=3)
302	
303	    TODO: So that this method generalizes to n-sided polygons, we can use the Waschpress points as the generalized
304	    barycentric coordinates, which is valid for convex polygons.
305	
306	    Parameters
307	    ----------
308	        nodes : numpy.ndarray
309	            Polygon verties per query of shape (M, 3, 2/3) where M is the number of query points. The second dimension corresponds to the number
310	            of vertices
311	            The last dimension can be either 2 or 3, where 3 corresponds to the (x, y, z) coordinates of each vertex and 2 corresponds to the
312	            (lon, lat) coordinates of each vertex.
313	
314	        points : numpy.ndarray
315	            Spherical coordinates of the point (M,2/3) where M is the number of query points.
316	
317	    Returns
318	    -------
319	    numpy.ndarray
320	        Barycentric coordinates corresponding to each vertex.
321	
322	    """
323	    M, K = nodes.shape[:2]
324	
325	    vi0 = nodes[:, 0, :]  # (M,K,2)
326	    vi1 = nodes[:, 1, :]  # (M,K,2)
327	    vi2 = nodes[:, 2, :]  # (M,K,2)
328	
329	    a = _triangle_area(vi0, vi1, vi2)  # (M,K)
330	
331	    P = points
332	    a0 = _triangle_area(P, vi1, vi2)
333	    a1 = _triangle_area(P, vi2, vi0)
334	    a2 = _triangle_area(P, vi0, vi1)
335	
336	    bcoords = np.zeros((M, K))
337	    bcoords[:, 0] = a0 / a
338	    bcoords[:, 1] = a1 / a
339	    bcoords[:, 2] = a2 / a
340	
341	    return bcoords

344	def _latlon_rad_to_xyz(
345	    lat,
346	    lon,
347	):
348	    """Converts Spherical latitude and longitude coordinates into Cartesian x,
349	    y, z coordinates.
350	    """
351	    x = np.cos(lon) * np.cos(lat)
352	    y = np.sin(lon) * np.cos(lat)
353	    z = np.sin(lat)
354	
355	    return x, y, z

57	    """

59	    the axes, and inserts mock dimensions of size 1 for any axes not present in the DataArray.
60	    """
61	    ax_dims = [(get_axis_from_dim_name(xgcm_grid.axes, dim), dim) for dim in da.dims]

66	        return da.rename({old_dim: f"mock{axis}" for old_dim, axis in zip(da.dims, _FIELD_DATA_ORDERING, strict=True)})
67	
68	    # All dimensions must be associated with an axis in the grid
69	    if any(ax_dim[0] is None for ax_dim in ax_dims):
70	        raise ValueError(
71	            f"DataArray {da.name!r} with dims {da.dims} has dimensions that are not associated with a direction on the provided grid."
72	        )
73	
74	    axes_not_in_field = set(_FIELD_DATA_ORDERING) - set(ax_dim[0] for ax_dim in ax_dims)
75	
76	    mock_dims_to_create = {}
77	    for ax in axes_not_in_field:
78	        mock_dims_to_create[f"mock{ax}"] = 1
79	        ax_dims.append((ax, f"mock{ax}"))
80	
81	    if mock_dims_to_create:
82	        da = da.expand_dims(mock_dims_to_create, create_index_for_new_dim=False)
83	
84	    ax_dims = sorted(ax_dims, key=lambda x: _FIELD_DATA_ORDERING.index(x[0]))
85	
86	    return da.transpose(*[ax_dim[1] for ax_dim in ax_dims])

514	def _convert_center_pos_to_fpoint(
515	    *,
516	    index: int,
517	    bcoord: float,
518	    xgcm_position: ptyping.XgcmAxisPosition,
519	    f_points_xgcm_position: ptyping.XgcmAxisPosition,
520	) -> tuple[int, float]:
521	    """Converts a physical position relative to the cell edges defined in the grid to be relative to the center point.
522	
523	    This is used to "localize" a position to be relative to the staggered grid at which the field is defined, so that
524	    it can be easily interpolated.
525	
526	    This also handles different model input cell edges and centers are staggered in different directions (e.g., with NEMO and MITgcm).
527	    """
528	    if xgcm_position != "center":  # Data is already defined on the F points
529	        return index, bcoord
530	
531	    bcoord = bcoord - 0.5
532	    if bcoord < 0:
533	        bcoord += 1.0
534	        index -= 1
535	
536	    # Correct relative to the f-point position
537	    if f_points_xgcm_position in ["inner", "right"]:
538	        index += 1
539	
540	    return index, bcoord

193	                self._zlow = np.zeros_like(self._xlow)
194	                self._zhigh = np.zeros_like(self._xlow)
195	
196	        # Generate the mapping from the hash indices to unstructured grid elements
197	        self._hash_table = self._initialize_hash_table()
198	
199	    def _initialize_hash_table(self):
200	        """Create a mapping that relates unstructured grid faces to hash indices by determining
201	        which faces overlap with which hash cells
202	        """
203	        # Quantize the bounding box in each direction
204	        xqlow, yqlow, zqlow = quantize_coordinates(
205	            self._xlow,
206	            self._ylow,
207	            self._zlow,
208	            self._xmin,
209	            self._xmax,
210	            self._ymin,
211	            self._ymax,
212	            self._zmin,
213	            self._zmax,
214	            self._bitwidth,
215	        )
216	
217	        xqhigh, yqhigh, zqhigh = quantize_coordinates(
218	            self._xhigh,
219	            self._yhigh,
220	            self._zhigh,
221	            self._xmin,
222	            self._xmax,
223	            self._ymin,
224	            self._ymax,
225	            self._zmin,
226	            self._zmax,
227	            self._bitwidth,
228	        )
229	        xqlow = xqlow.ravel().astype(np.int32, copy=False)
230	        yqlow = yqlow.ravel().astype(np.int32, copy=False)
231	        zqlow = zqlow.ravel().astype(np.int32, copy=False)
232	        xqhigh = xqhigh.ravel().astype(np.int32, copy=False)
233	        yqhigh = yqhigh.ravel().astype(np.int32, copy=False)
234	        zqhigh = zqhigh.ravel().astype(np.int32, copy=False)
235	        nx = (xqhigh - xqlow + 1).astype(np.int32, copy=False)
236	        ny = (yqhigh - yqlow + 1).astype(np.int32, copy=False)
237	        nz = (zqhigh - zqlow + 1).astype(np.int32, copy=False)
238	        num_hash_per_face = (nx * ny * nz).astype(
239	            np.int32, copy=False
240	        )  # Since nx, ny, nz are in the 10-bit range, their product fits in int32
241	        total_hash_entries = int(num_hash_per_face.sum())
242	
243	        # Preallocate output arrays
244	        morton_codes = np.zeros(total_hash_entries, dtype=np.uint32)
245	
246	        # Compute the j, i indices corresponding to each hash entry
247	        nface = np.size(self._xlow)
248	        face_ids = np.repeat(np.arange(nface, dtype=np.int32), num_hash_per_face)
249	        offsets = np.concatenate(([0], np.cumsum(num_hash_per_face))).astype(np.int32)[:-1]
250	
251	        valid = num_hash_per_face != 0
252	        if not np.any(valid):
253	            # nothing to do
254	            pass
255	        else:
256	            # Grab only valid faces to avoid empty arrays
257	            nx_v = np.asarray(nx[valid], dtype=np.int32)
258	            ny_v = np.asarray(ny[valid], dtype=np.int32)
259	            nz_v = np.asarray(nz[valid], dtype=np.int32)
260	            xlow_v = np.asarray(xqlow[valid], dtype=np.int32)
261	            ylow_v = np.asarray(yqlow[valid], dtype=np.int32)
262	            zlow_v = np.asarray(zqlow[valid], dtype=np.int32)
263	            starts_v = np.asarray(offsets[valid], dtype=np.int32)
264	
265	            # Count of elements per valid face (should match num_hash_per_face[valid])
266	            counts = (nx_v * ny_v * nz_v).astype(np.int32)
267	            total = int(counts.sum())
268	
269	            # Map each global element to its face and output position
270	            start_for_elem = np.repeat(starts_v, counts)  # shape (total,)
271	
272	            # Intra-face linear index for each element (0..counts_i-1)
273	            # Offsets per face within the concatenation of valid faces:
274	            face_starts_local = np.cumsum(np.r_[0, counts[:-1]])
275	            intra = np.arange(total, dtype=np.int32) - np.repeat(face_starts_local, counts)
276	
277	            # Derive (zi, yi, xi) from intra using per-face sizes
278	            ny_nz = np.repeat(ny_v * nz_v, counts)
279	            nz_rep = np.repeat(nz_v, counts)
280	
281	            xi = intra // ny_nz
282	            rem = intra % ny_nz
283	            yi = rem // nz_rep
284	            zi = rem % nz_rep
285	
286	            # Add per-face lows
287	            x0 = np.repeat(xlow_v, counts)
288	            y0 = np.repeat(ylow_v, counts)
289	            z0 = np.repeat(zlow_v, counts)
290	
291	            xq = x0 + xi
292	            yq = y0 + yi
293	            zq = z0 + zi
294	
295	            # Vectorized morton encode for all elements at once
296	            codes_all = _encode_quantized_morton3d(xq, yq, zq)
297	
298	            # Scatter into the preallocated output using computed absolute indices
299	            out_idx = start_for_elem + intra
300	            morton_codes[out_idx] = codes_all
301	
302	        # Sort face indices by morton code
303	        order = np.argsort(morton_codes)
304	        morton_codes_sorted = morton_codes[order]
305	        face_sorted = face_ids[order]
306	        j_sorted, i_sorted = np.unravel_index(face_sorted, self._xlow.shape)
307	
308	        # Get a list of unique morton codes and their corresponding starts and counts (CSR format)
309	        keys, starts, counts = np.unique(morton_codes_sorted, return_index=True, return_counts=True)
310	
311	        hash_table = {
312	            "keys": keys,
313	            "starts": starts,
314	            "counts": counts,
315	            "i": i_sorted,
316	            "j": j_sorted,
317	        }
318	        return hash_table

320	    def query(self, y, x):
321	        """
322	        Queries the hash table and finds the closes face in the source grid for each coordinate pair.
323	
324	        Parameters
325	        ----------
326	        y : array_like
327	            y-coordinates in degrees (lat) to query of shape (N,) where N is the number of queries.
328	        x : array_like
329	            x-coordinates in degrees (lon) to query of shape (N,) where N is the number of queries.
330	
331	        Returns
332	        -------
333	        j : ndarray, shape (N,)
334	            j-indices of the located face in the source grid for each query. If no face was found, GRID_SEARCH_ERROR is returned.
335	        i : ndarray, shape (N,)
336	            i-indices of the located face in the source grid for each query. If no face was found, GRID_SEARCH_ERROR is returned.
337	        coords : ndarray, shape (N, 2)
338	            The local coordinates (xsi, eta) of the located face in the source grid for each query.
339	            If no face was found, (-1.0, -1.0)
340	        """
341	        keys = self._hash_table["keys"]
342	        starts = self._hash_table["starts"]
343	        counts = self._hash_table["counts"]
344	        i = self._hash_table["i"]
345	        j = self._hash_table["j"]
346	
347	        y = np.asarray(y)
348	        x = np.asarray(x)
349	        if self._source_grid._mesh == "spherical":
350	            # Convert coords to Cartesian coordinates (x, y, z)
351	            lat = np.deg2rad(y)
352	            lon = np.deg2rad(x)
353	            qx, qy, qz = _latlon_rad_to_xyz(lat, lon)
354	        else:
355	            # For Cartesian grids, use the coordinates directly
356	            qx = x
357	            qy = y
358	            qz = np.zeros_like(qx)
359	
360	        query_codes = _encode_morton3d(
361	            qx, qy, qz, self._xmin, self._xmax, self._ymin, self._ymax, self._zmin, self._zmax
362	        ).ravel()
363	        num_queries = query_codes.size
364	
365	        # Locate each query in the unique key array
366	        pos = np.searchsorted(keys, query_codes)  # pos is shape (num_queries,)
367	
368	        # Valid hits: inside range with finite query coordinates and query codes give exact morton code match.
369	        valid = (pos < len(keys)) & np.isfinite(x) & np.isfinite(y)
370	        # Clip pos to valid range to avoid out-of-bounds indexing
371	        pos = np.clip(pos, 0, len(keys) - 1)
372	        # Further filter out false positives from searchsorted by checking for exact code match
373	        valid[valid] &= query_codes[valid] == keys[pos[valid]]
374	
375	        # Pre-allocate i and j indices of the best match for each query
376	        # Default values to -1 (no match case)
377	        j_best = np.full(num_queries, GRID_SEARCH_ERROR, dtype=np.int32)
378	        i_best = np.full(num_queries, GRID_SEARCH_ERROR, dtype=np.int32)
379	
380	        # How many matches each query has; hit_counts[i] is the number of hits for query i
381	        hit_counts = np.where(valid, counts[pos], 0).astype(np.int32)  # has shape (num_queries,)
382	        if hit_counts.sum() == 0:
383	            return (
384	                j_best.reshape(query_codes.shape),
385	                i_best.reshape(query_codes.shape),
386	                np.full((num_queries, self._coord_dim), -1.0, dtype=np.float32),
387	            )
388	
389	        # Now, for each query, we need to gather the candidate (j,i) indices from the hash table
390	        # Each j,i pair needs to be repeated hit_counts[i] times, only when there are hits.
391	
392	        # Boolean array for keeping track of which queries have candidates
393	        has_hits = hit_counts > 0  # shape (num_queries,), True for queries that had candidates
394	
395	        # A quick lookup array that maps all candindates back to its query index
396	        q_index_for_candidate = np.repeat(
397	            np.arange(num_queries, dtype=np.int32), hit_counts
398	        )  # shape (hit_counts.sum(),)
399	        # Map all candidates to positions in the hash table
400	        hash_positions = pos[q_index_for_candidate]  # shape (hit_counts.sum(),)
401	
402	        # Now that we have the positions in the hash table for each table, we can gather the (j,i) pairs for each candidate
403	        # We do this in a vectorized way by using a CSR-like approach
404	        # starts[pos[q_index_for_candidate]] gives the starting point in the hash table for each candidate
405	        # hit_counts gives the number of candidates for each query
406	
407	        # We need to build an array that gives the offset within each query's candidates
408	        offsets = np.concatenate(([0], np.cumsum(hit_counts))).astype(np.int32)  # shape (num_queries+1,)
409	        total = int(offsets[-1])  # total number of candidates across all queries
410	
411	        # Now, for each candidate, we need a simple array that tells us its "local candidate id" within its query
412	        # This way, we can easily take the starts[pos[q_index_for_candidate]] and add this local id to get the absolute index
413	        # We calculate this by computing the "global candidate number" (0..total-1) and subtracting the offsets of the corresponding query
414	        # This gives us an array that goes from 0..hit_counts[i]-1 for each query i
415	        intra = np.arange(total, dtype=np.int32) - np.repeat(offsets[:-1], hit_counts)  # shape (hit_counts.sum(),)
416	
417	        # starts[pos[q_index_for_candidate]] + intra gives a list of positions in the hash table that we can
418	        # use to quickly gather the (i,j) pairs for each query
419	        source_idx = starts[hash_positions].astype(np.int32) + intra
420	
421	        # Gather all candidate (j,i) pairs in one shot
422	        j_all = j[source_idx]
423	        i_all = i[source_idx]
424	
425	        # Now we need to construct arrays that repeats the y and x coordinates for each candidate
426	        # to enable vectorized point-in-cell checks
427	        y_rep = np.repeat(y, hit_counts)  # shape (hit_counts.sum(),)
428	        x_rep = np.repeat(x, hit_counts)  # shape (hit_counts.sum(),)
429	
430	        # For each query we perform a point in cell check.
431	        is_in_face, coordinates = self._point_in_cell(self._source_grid, y_rep, x_rep, j_all, i_all)
432	
433	        coords_best = np.full((num_queries, coordinates.shape[1]), -1.0, dtype=np.float32)
434	
435	        # For each query that has hits, we need to find the first candidate that was inside the face
436	        f_indices = np.flatnonzero(is_in_face)  # Indices of all faces that contained the point
437	        # For each true position, find which query it belongs to by searching offsets
438	        # Query index q satisfies offsets[q] <= pos < offsets[q+1].
439	        q = np.searchsorted(offsets[1:], f_indices, side="right")
440	
441	        uniq_q, q_idx = np.unique(q, return_index=True)
442	        keep = has_hits[uniq_q]
443	
444	        if keep.any():
445	            uniq_q = uniq_q[keep]
446	            pos_first = f_indices[q_idx[keep]]
447	
448	            # Directly scatter: the code wants the first True inside each slice
449	            j_best[uniq_q] = j_all[pos_first]
450	            i_best[uniq_q] = i_all[pos_first]
451	            coords_best[uniq_q] = coordinates[pos_first]
452	
453	        return (
454	            j_best.reshape(query_codes.shape),
455	            i_best.reshape(query_codes.shape),
456	            coords_best.reshape((num_queries, coordinates.shape[1])),
457	        )

460	def _dilate_bits(n):
461	    """
462	    Takes a 10-bit integer n, in range [0,1023], and "dilates" its bits so that
463	    there are two zeros between each bit of n in the result.
464	
465	    This is a preparation step for building a 3D Morton code:
466	    - One axis (x, y, or z) is dilated like this.
467	    - Then the three dilated coordinates are bitwise interleaved
468	      to produce the full 30-bit Morton code.
469	
470	    Example:
471	        Input n:  b9 b8 b7 b6 b5 b4 b3 b2 b1 b0
472	        Output:   b9 0 0 b8 0 0 b7 0 0 ... b0 0 0
473	    """
474	    n = np.asarray(n, dtype=np.uint32)
475	
476	    # Step 1: Keep only the lowest 10 bits of n
477	    # Mask = 0x3FF = binary 11 1111 1111
478	    n &= np.uint32(0x000003FF)
479	
480	    # Step 2: First spreading stage
481	    # Shift left by 16 and OR with original.
482	    # This spreads the bits apart, but introduces overlaps.
483	    # Mask 0xff0000ff clears out the unwanted overlaps.
484	    n = (n | (n << np.uint32(16))) & np.uint32(0xFF0000FF)
485	
486	    # Step 3: Second spreading stage
487	    # Similar idea: shift left by 8, OR, then mask.
488	    # Now the bits are further separated.
489	    n = (n | (n << np.uint32(8))) & np.uint32(0x0300F00F)
490	
491	    # Step 4: Third spreading stage
492	    # Shift by 4, OR, mask again.
493	    # At this point, there are 1 or 2 zeros between many of the bits.
494	    n = (n | (n << np.uint32(4))) & np.uint32(0x030C30C3)
495	
496	    # Step 5: Final spreading stage
497	    # Shift by 2, OR, mask.
498	    # After this, each original bit is isolated with exactly two zeros
499	    # between it and the next bit, ready for 3D Morton interleaving.
500	    n = (n | (n << np.uint32(2))) & np.uint32(0x09249249)
501	
502	    # Return the dilated value.
503	    return n

506	def _find_degenerate_xgrid_faces(x, y, z, threshold_factor=10):
507	    """Identify faces in structured grids that potentially span large portions of
508	    the underlying hash grid (e.g., due to the mesh being incomplete, with 0.0 stored in missing lon/lat points). Such degenerate faces can result in high memory requirements
509	    for the hash table.
510	
511	    Detection is based on the maximum great-circle edge length of each cell.  A cell
512	    is flagged as degenerate when its longest edge exceeds ``threshold_factor`` multiplied by
513	    the 99th percentile of all edge lengths.
514	
515	    Parameters
516	    ----------
517	    x, y, z : ndarray, shape (ny, nx)
518	        Unit-sphere Cartesian coordinates of the grid nodes.
519	    threshold_factor : float, optional
520	        Multiplier applied to the 99th-percentile edge length to set the threshold.
521	        Default is 10.
522	
523	    Returns
524	    -------
525	    degenerate : ndarray of bool, shape (ny-1, nx-1)
526	        True for each cell whose maximum edge length exceeds the threshold.
527	    """
528	
529	    # Chord length between two sets of points on the unit sphere, shape (ny-1, nx-1)
530	    def _chord(p1, p2):
531	        return np.sqrt(((p1 - p2) ** 2).sum(axis=-1))
532	
533	    pts = np.stack([x, y, z], axis=-1)
534	    c00, c01 = pts[:-1, :-1], pts[:-1, 1:]
535	    c10, c11 = pts[1:, :-1], pts[1:, 1:]
536	
537	    # Maximum chord across all four edges and both diagonals
538	    max_chord = np.maximum.reduce(
539	        [
540	            _chord(c00, c01),
541	            _chord(c10, c11),
542	            _chord(c00, c10),
543	            _chord(c01, c11),
544	            _chord(c00, c11),
545	            _chord(c01, c10),
546	        ]
547	    )
548	
549	    threshold = threshold_factor * np.percentile(max_chord, 99)
550	    return max_chord > threshold
551

553	def quantize_coordinates(x, y, z, xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax, bitwidth=1023):
554	    """
555	    Normalize (x, y, z) to [0, 1] over their bounding box, then quantize to 10 bits each (0..1023).
556	
557	    Parameters
558	    ----------
559	    x, y, z : array_like
560	        Input coordinates to quantize. Can be scalars or arrays (broadcasting applies).
561	    xmin, xmax : float
562	        Minimum and maximum bounds for x coordinate.
563	    ymin, ymax : float
564	        Minimum and maximum bounds for y coordinate.
565	    zmin, zmax : float
566	        Minimum and maximum bounds for z coordinate.
567	
568	    Returns
569	    -------
570	    xq, yq, zq : ndarray, dtype=uint32
571	        The quantized coordinates, each in range [0, 1023], same shape as the broadcasted input coordinates.
572	    """
573	    # Convert inputs to ndarray for consistent dtype/ufunc behavior.
574	    x = np.asarray(x)
575	    y = np.asarray(y)
576	    z = np.asarray(z)
577	
578	    # --- 1) Normalize each coordinate to [0, 1] over its bounding box. ---
579	    # Compute denominators once (avoid division by zero if bounds equal).
580	    dx = xmax - xmin
581	    dy = ymax - ymin
582	    dz = zmax - zmin
583	
584	    # Normalize to [0,1]; if a range is degenerate, map to 0 to avoid NaN/inf.
585	    with np.errstate(invalid="ignore"):
586	        xn = np.where(dx != 0, (x - xmin) / dx, 0.0)
587	        yn = np.where(dy != 0, (y - ymin) / dy, 0.0)
588	        zn = np.where(dz != 0, (z - zmin) / dz, 0.0)
589	
590	    # --- 2) Quantize to (0..bitwidth). ---
591	    # Multiply by bitwidth, round down, and clip to be safe against slight overshoot.
592	    xq = np.clip((xn * bitwidth).astype(np.uint32), 0, bitwidth)
593	    yq = np.clip((yn * bitwidth).astype(np.uint32), 0, bitwidth)
594	    zq = np.clip((zn * bitwidth).astype(np.uint32), 0, bitwidth)
595	
596	    return xq, yq, zq
597

599	def _encode_quantized_morton3d(xq, yq, zq):
600	    xq = np.asarray(xq)
601	    yq = np.asarray(yq)
602	    zq = np.asarray(zq)
603	
604	    # --- 3) Bit-dilate each 10-bit number so each bit is separated by two zeros. ---
605	    # _dilate_bits maps:  b9..b0  ->  b9 0 0 b8 0 0 ... b0 0 0
606	    dx3 = _dilate_bits(xq).astype(np.uint32)
607	    dy3 = _dilate_bits(yq).astype(np.uint32)
608	    dz3 = _dilate_bits(zq).astype(np.uint32)
609	
610	    # --- 4) Interleave the dilated bits into a single Morton code. ---
611	    # Bit layout (from LSB upward): x0,y0,z0, x1,y1,z1, ..., x9,y9,z9
612	    # We shift z's bits by 2, y's by 1, x stays at 0, then OR them together.
613	    # Cast to a wide type before shifting/OR to be safe when arrays are used.
614	    code = (dz3 << 2) | (dy3 << 1) | dx3
615	
616	    # Since our compact type fits in 30 bits, uint32 is enough.
617	    return code.astype(np.uint32)
618

620	def _encode_morton3d(x, y, z, xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax, bitwidth=1023):
621	    """
622	    Quantize (x, y, z) to 10 bits each (0..1023), dilate the bits so there are
623	    two zeros between successive bits, and interleave them into a 3D Morton code.
624	
625	    Parameters
626	    ----------
627	    x, y, z : array_like
628	        Input coordinates to encode. Can be scalars or arrays (broadcasting applies).
629	    xmin, xmax : float
630	        Minimum and maximum bounds for x coordinate.
631	    ymin, ymax : float
632	        Minimum and maximum bounds for y coordinate.
633	    zmin, zmax : float
634	        Minimum and maximum bounds for z coordinate.
635	
636	    Returns
637	    -------
638	    code : ndarray, dtype=uint32
639	        The resulting Morton codes, same shape as the broadcasted input coordinates.
640	
641	    Notes
642	    -----
643	    - Works with scalars or NumPy arrays (broadcasting applies).
644	    - Output is up to 30 bits returned as uint32.
645	    """
646	    # Convert inputs to ndarray for consistent dtype/ufunc behavior.
647	    x = np.asarray(x)
648	    y = np.asarray(y)
649	    z = np.asarray(z)
650	
651	    xq, yq, zq = quantize_coordinates(x, y, z, xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax, bitwidth)
652	
653	    # --- 3) Bit-dilate each 10-bit number so each bit is separated by two zeros. ---
654	    # _dilate_bits maps:  b9..b0  ->  b9 0 0 b8 0 0 ... b0 0 0
655	    dx3 = _dilate_bits(xq).astype(np.uint32)
656	    dy3 = _dilate_bits(yq).astype(np.uint32)
657	    dz3 = _dilate_bits(zq).astype(np.uint32)
658	
659	    # --- 4) Interleave the dilated bits into a single Morton code. ---
660	    # Bit layout (from LSB upward): x0,y0,z0, x1,y1,z1, ..., x9,y9,z9
661	    # We shift z's bits by 2, y's by 1, x stays at 0, then OR them together.
662	    # Cast to a wide type before shifting/OR to be safe when arrays are used.
663	    code = (dz3 << 2) | (dy3 << 1) | dx3
664	
665	    # Since our compact type fits in 30 bits, uint32 is enough.
666	    return code.astype(np.uint32)

37	def _get_corner_data_Agrid(
38	    data: np.ndarray | xr.DataArray,
39	    ti: int,
40	    zi: int,
41	    yi: int,
42	    xi: int,
43	    lenT: int,  # noqa: N803
44	    lenZ: int,  # noqa: N803
45	    npart: int,
46	    axis_dim: dict[ptyping.XgridAxis, str],
47	) -> np.ndarray:
48	    """Helper function to get the corner data for a given A-grid field and position."""
49	    # Time coordinates: 8 points at ti, then 8 points at ti+1
50	    if lenT == 1:
51	        ti = np.repeat(ti, lenZ * 4)
52	    else:
53	        ti_1 = np.clip(ti + 1, 0, data.shape[0] - 1)
54	        ti = np.concatenate([np.repeat(ti, lenZ * 4), np.repeat(ti_1, lenZ * 4)])
55	
56	    # Z coordinates: 4 points at zi, 4 at zi+1, repeated for both time levels
57	    if lenZ == 1:
58	        zi = np.repeat(zi, lenT * 4)
59	    else:
60	        zi_1 = np.clip(zi + 1, 0, data.shape[1] - 1)
61	        zi = np.tile(np.array([zi, zi, zi, zi, zi_1, zi_1, zi_1, zi_1]).flatten(), lenT)
62	
63	    # Y coordinates: [yi, yi, yi+1, yi+1] for each spatial point, repeated for time/z
64	    yi_1 = np.clip(yi + 1, 0, data.shape[2] - 1)
65	    yi = np.tile(np.array([yi, yi, yi_1, yi_1]).flatten(), lenT * lenZ)
66	
67	    # X coordinates: [xi, xi+1, xi, xi+1] for each spatial point, repeated for time/z
68	    xi_1 = np.clip(xi + 1, 0, data.shape[3] - 1)
69	    xi = np.tile(np.array([xi, xi_1]).flatten(), lenT * lenZ * 2)
70	
71	    # Create DataArrays for indexing
72	    selection_dict = {}
73	    if "X" in axis_dim:
74	        selection_dict[axis_dim["X"]] = xr.DataArray(xi, dims=("points"))
75	    if "Y" in axis_dim:
76	        selection_dict[axis_dim["Y"]] = xr.DataArray(yi, dims=("points"))
77	    if "Z" in axis_dim:
78	        selection_dict[axis_dim["Z"]] = xr.DataArray(zi, dims=("points"))
79	    if "time" in data.dims:
80	        selection_dict["time"] = xr.DataArray(ti, dims=("points"))
81	
82	    return data.isel(selection_dict).data.reshape(lenT, lenZ, 2, 2, npart)

85	def _get_offsets_dictionary(grid):
86	    offsets = {}
87	    for axis in ["X", "Y"]:
88	        axis_coords = grid.xgcm_grid.axes[axis].coords.keys()
89	        offsets[axis] = 1 if "right" in axis_coords else 0
90	    if "Z" in grid.xgcm_grid.axes:
91	        axis_coords = grid.xgcm_grid.axes["Z"].coords.keys()
92	        offsets["Z"] = 1 if "right" in axis_coords else 0
93	    else:
94	        offsets["Z"] = 0
95	    return offsets

98	def XLinear(
99	    particle_positions: dict[str, float | np.ndarray],
100	    grid_positions: dict[XgridAxis, dict[str, int | float | np.ndarray]],
101	    field: Field,
102	):
103	    """Trilinear interpolation on a regular grid."""
104	    xi, xsi = grid_positions["X"]["index"], grid_positions["X"]["bcoord"]
105	    yi, eta = grid_positions["Y"]["index"], grid_positions["Y"]["bcoord"]
106	    zi, zeta = grid_positions["Z"]["index"], grid_positions["Z"]["bcoord"]
107	    ti, tau = grid_positions["T"]["index"], grid_positions["T"]["bcoord"]
108	
109	    axis_dim = field.grid.get_axis_dim_mapping(field.data.dims)
110	    data = field.data
111	
112	    lenT = 2 if np.any(tau > 0) else 1
113	    lenZ = 2 if np.any(zeta > 0) else 1
114	
115	    corner_data = _get_corner_data_Agrid(data, ti, zi, yi, xi, lenT, lenZ, len(xsi), axis_dim)
116	
117	    if lenT == 2:
118	        tau = tau[np.newaxis, :]
119	        corner_data = corner_data[0, :] * (1 - tau) + corner_data[1, :] * tau
120	    else:
121	        corner_data = corner_data[0, :]
122	
123	    if lenZ == 2:
124	        zeta = zeta[np.newaxis, :]
125	        corner_data = corner_data[0, :] * (1 - zeta) + corner_data[1, :] * zeta
126	    else:
127	        corner_data = corner_data[0, :]
128	
129	    value = (
130	        (1 - xsi) * (1 - eta) * corner_data[0, 0, :]
131	        + xsi * (1 - eta) * corner_data[0, 1, :]
132	        + (1 - xsi) * eta * corner_data[1, 0, :]
133	        + xsi * eta * corner_data[1, 1, :]
134	    )
135	    return value.compute() if is_dask_collection(value) else value

147	def XLinear_Velocity(
148	    particle_positions: dict[str, float | np.ndarray],
149	    grid_positions: dict[XgridAxis, dict[str, int | float | np.ndarray]],
150	    vectorfield: VectorField,
151	):
152	    """Trilinear interpolation on a regular grid for VectorFields of velocity."""
153	    u = XLinear(particle_positions, grid_positions, vectorfield.U)
154	    v = XLinear(particle_positions, grid_positions, vectorfield.V)
155	    if vectorfield.grid._mesh == "spherical":
156	        u /= 1852 * 60 * np.cos(np.deg2rad(particle_positions["lat"]))
157	        v /= 1852 * 60
158	
159	    if vectorfield.W:
160	        w = XLinear(particle_positions, grid_positions, vectorfield.W)
161	    else:
162	        w = 0.0
163	    return u, v, w

166	def CGrid_Velocity(
167	    particle_positions: dict[str, float | np.ndarray],
168	    grid_positions: dict[XgridAxis, dict[str, int | float | np.ndarray]],
169	    vectorfield: VectorField,
170	):
171	    """
172	    Interpolation kernel for velocity fields on a C-Grid.
173	    Following Delandmeter and Van Sebille (2019), velocity fields should be interpolated
174	    only in the direction of the grid cell faces.
175	    """
176	    xi, xsi = grid_positions["X"]["index"], grid_positions["X"]["bcoord"]
177	    yi, eta = grid_positions["Y"]["index"], grid_positions["Y"]["bcoord"]
178	    zi, zeta = grid_positions["Z"]["index"], grid_positions["Z"]["bcoord"]
179	    ti, tau = grid_positions["T"]["index"], grid_positions["T"]["bcoord"]
180	    lon = particle_positions["lon"]
181	
182	    U = vectorfield.U.data
183	    V = vectorfield.V.data
184	    grid = vectorfield.grid
185	    offsets = _get_offsets_dictionary(grid)
186	    tdim, zdim, ydim, xdim = U.shape[0], U.shape[1], U.shape[2], U.shape[3]
187	    lenT = 2 if np.any(tau > 0) else 1
188	
189	    if grid.lon.ndim == 1:
190	        px = np.array([grid.lon[xi], grid.lon[xi + 1], grid.lon[xi + 1], grid.lon[xi]])
191	        py = np.array([grid.lat[yi], grid.lat[yi], grid.lat[yi + 1], grid.lat[yi + 1]])
192	    else:
193	        px = np.array([grid.lon[yi, xi], grid.lon[yi, xi + 1], grid.lon[yi + 1, xi + 1], grid.lon[yi + 1, xi]])
194	        py = np.array([grid.lat[yi, xi], grid.lat[yi, xi + 1], grid.lat[yi + 1, xi + 1], grid.lat[yi + 1, xi]])
195	
196	    if grid._mesh == "spherical":
197	        px = ((px + 180.0) % 360.0) - 180.0
198	        px[1:] = np.where(px[1:] - px[0] > 180, px[1:] - 360, px[1:])
199	        px[1:] = np.where(-px[1:] + px[0] > 180, px[1:] + 360, px[1:])
200	    c1 = i_u._geodetic_distance(
201	        py[0], py[1], px[0], px[1], grid._mesh, np.einsum("ij,ji->i", i_u.phi2D_lin(0.0, xsi), py)
202	    )
203	    c2 = i_u._geodetic_distance(
204	        py[1], py[2], px[1], px[2], grid._mesh, np.einsum("ij,ji->i", i_u.phi2D_lin(eta, 1.0), py)
205	    )
206	    c3 = i_u._geodetic_distance(
207	        py[2], py[3], px[2], px[3], grid._mesh, np.einsum("ij,ji->i", i_u.phi2D_lin(1.0, xsi), py)
208	    )
209	    c4 = i_u._geodetic_distance(
210	        py[3], py[0], px[3], px[0], grid._mesh, np.einsum("ij,ji->i", i_u.phi2D_lin(eta, 0.0), py)
211	    )
212	
213	    def _create_selection_dict(dims, zdir=False):
214	        """Helper function to create DataArrays for indexing."""
215	        axis_dim = grid.get_axis_dim_mapping(dims)
216	        selection_dict = {
217	            axis_dim["X"]: xr.DataArray(xi_full, dims=("points")),
218	            axis_dim["Y"]: xr.DataArray(yi_full, dims=("points")),
219	        }
220	
221	        # Time coordinates: 2 points at ti, then 2 points at ti+1
222	        if "time" in dims:
223	            if lenT == 1:
224	                ti_full = np.repeat(ti, 2)
225	            else:
226	                ti_1 = np.clip(ti + 1, 0, tdim - 1)
227	                ti_full = np.concatenate([np.repeat(ti, 2), np.repeat(ti_1, 2)])
228	            selection_dict["time"] = xr.DataArray(ti_full, dims=("points"))
229	
230	        if "Z" in axis_dim:
231	            if zdir:
232	                # Z coordinates: 1 point at zi and 1 point at zi+1 repeated for lenT time levels
233	                zi_0 = np.clip(zi + offsets["Z"], 0, zdim - 1)
234	                zi_1 = np.clip(zi + offsets["Z"] + 1, 0, zdim - 1)
235	                zi_full = np.tile(np.array([zi_0, zi_1]).flatten(), lenT)
236	            else:
237	                # Z coordinates: 2 points at zi, repeated for lenT time levels
238	                zi_full = np.repeat(zi, lenT * 2)
239	            selection_dict[axis_dim["Z"]] = xr.DataArray(zi_full, dims=("points"))
240	
241	        return selection_dict
242	
243	    def _compute_corner_data(data, selection_dict) -> np.ndarray:
244	        """Helper function to load and reduce corner data over time dimension if needed."""
245	        corner_data = data.isel(selection_dict).data.reshape(lenT, 2, len(xsi))
246	
247	        if lenT == 2:
248	            tau_full = tau[np.newaxis, :]
249	            corner_data = corner_data[0, :] * (1 - tau_full) + corner_data[1, :] * tau_full
250	        else:
251	            corner_data = corner_data[0, :]
252	        return corner_data
253	
254	    # Compute U velocity
255	    yi_o = np.clip(yi + offsets["Y"], 0, ydim - 1)
256	    yi_full = np.tile(np.array([yi_o, yi_o]).flatten(), lenT)
257	
258	    xi_1 = np.clip(xi + 1, 0, xdim - 1)
259	    xi_full = np.tile(np.array([xi, xi_1]).flatten(), lenT)
260	
261	    selection_dict = _create_selection_dict(U.dims)
262	    corner_data = _compute_corner_data(U, selection_dict)
263	
264	    U0 = corner_data[0, :] * c4
265	    U1 = corner_data[1, :] * c2
266	    Uvel = (1 - xsi) * U0 + xsi * U1
267	
268	    # Compute V velocity
269	    yi_1 = np.clip(yi + 1, 0, ydim - 1)
270	    yi_full = np.tile(np.array([yi, yi_1]).flatten(), lenT)
271	
272	    xi_o = np.clip(xi + offsets["X"], 0, xdim - 1)
273	    xi_full = np.tile(np.array([xi_o, xi_o]).flatten(), lenT)
274	
275	    selection_dict = _create_selection_dict(V.dims)
276	    corner_data = _compute_corner_data(V, selection_dict)
277	
278	    V0 = corner_data[0, :] * c1
279	    V1 = corner_data[1, :] * c3
280	    Vvel = (1 - eta) * V0 + eta * V1
281	
282	    if grid._mesh == "spherical":
283	        jac = i_u._compute_jacobian_determinant(py, px, eta, xsi) * 1852 * 60.0
284	    else:
285	        jac = i_u._compute_jacobian_determinant(py, px, eta, xsi)
286	
287	    u = (
288	        (-(1 - eta) * Uvel - (1 - xsi) * Vvel) * px[0]
289	        + ((1 - eta) * Uvel - xsi * Vvel) * px[1]
290	        + (eta * Uvel + xsi * Vvel) * px[2]
291	        + (-eta * Uvel + (1 - xsi) * Vvel) * px[3]
292	    ) / jac
293	    v = (
294	        (-(1 - eta) * Uvel - (1 - xsi) * Vvel) * py[0]
295	        + ((1 - eta) * Uvel - xsi * Vvel) * py[1]
296	        + (eta * Uvel + xsi * Vvel) * py[2]
297	        + (-eta * Uvel + (1 - xsi) * Vvel) * py[3]
298	    ) / jac
299	    if is_dask_collection(u):
300	        u = u.compute()
301	        v = v.compute()
302	
303	    if grid._mesh == "spherical":
304	        conversion = 1852 * 60.0 * np.cos(np.deg2rad(particle_positions["lat"]))
305	        u /= conversion
306	        v /= conversion
307	
308	    # check whether the grid conversion has been applied correctly
309	    xx = (1 - xsi) * (1 - eta) * px[0] + xsi * (1 - eta) * px[1] + xsi * eta * px[2] + (1 - xsi) * eta * px[3]
310	    dlon = xx - lon
311	    if grid._mesh == "spherical":
312	        dlon = ((dlon + 180.0) % 360.0) - 180.0
313	    u = np.where(np.abs(dlon / lon) > 1e-4, np.nan, u)
314	
315	    if vectorfield.W:
316	        W = vectorfield.W.data
317	
318	        # Y coordinates: yi+offset for each spatial point, repeated for time
319	        yi_o = np.clip(yi + offsets["Y"], 0, ydim - 1)
320	        yi_full = np.tile(yi_o, (lenT) * 2)
321	
322	        # X coordinates: xi+offset for each spatial point, repeated for time
323	        xi_o = np.clip(xi + offsets["X"], 0, xdim - 1)
324	        xi_full = np.tile(xi_o, (lenT) * 2)
325	
326	        selection_dict = _create_selection_dict(W.dims, zdir=True)
327	        corner_data = _compute_corner_data(W, selection_dict)
328	
329	        w = corner_data[0, :] * (1 - zeta) + corner_data[1, :] * zeta
330	        if is_dask_collection(w):
331	            w = w.compute()
332	    else:
333	        w = np.zeros_like(u)
334	
335	    return (u, v, w)

338	def CGrid_Tracer(
339	    particle_positions: dict[str, float | np.ndarray],
340	    grid_positions: dict[XgridAxis, dict[str, int | float | np.ndarray]],
341	    field: Field,
342	):
343	    """Interpolation kernel for tracer fields on a C-Grid.
344	
345	    Following Delandmeter and Van Sebille (2019), tracer fields should be interpolated
346	    constant over the grid cell
347	    """
348	    xi = grid_positions["X"]["index"]
349	    yi = grid_positions["Y"]["index"]
350	    zi = grid_positions["Z"]["index"]
351	    ti = grid_positions["T"]["index"]
352	    tau = grid_positions["T"]["bcoord"]
353	
354	    axis_dim = field.grid.get_axis_dim_mapping(field.data.dims)
355	    data = field.data
356	
357	    offsets = _get_offsets_dictionary(field.grid)
358	    zi = np.clip(zi + offsets["Z"], 0, data.shape[1] - 1)
359	    yi = np.clip(yi + offsets["Y"], 0, data.shape[2] - 1)
360	    xi = np.clip(xi + offsets["X"], 0, data.shape[3] - 1)
361	
362	    lenT = 2 if np.any(tau > 0) else 1
363	
364	    if lenT == 2:
365	        ti_1 = np.clip(ti + 1, 0, data.shape[0] - 1)
366	        ti = np.concatenate([np.repeat(ti), np.repeat(ti_1)])
367	        zi = np.tile(zi, (lenT) * 2)
368	        yi = np.tile(yi, (lenT) * 2)
369	        xi = np.tile(xi, (lenT) * 2)
370	
371	    # Create DataArrays for indexing
372	    selection_dict = {
373	        axis_dim["X"]: xr.DataArray(xi, dims=("points")),
374	        axis_dim["Y"]: xr.DataArray(yi, dims=("points")),
375	    }
376	    if "Z" in axis_dim:
377	        selection_dict[axis_dim["Z"]] = xr.DataArray(zi, dims=("points"))
378	    if "time" in field.data.dims:
379	        selection_dict["time"] = xr.DataArray(ti, dims=("points"))
380	
381	    value = data.isel(selection_dict).data.reshape(lenT, len(xi))
382	
383	    if lenT == 2:
384	        tau = tau[:, np.newaxis]
385	        value = value[0, :] * (1 - tau) + value[1, :] * tau
386	    else:
387	        value = value[0, :]
388	
389	    return value.compute() if is_dask_collection(value) else value

392	def _Spatialslip(
393	    particle_positions: dict[str, float | np.ndarray],
394	    grid_positions: dict[XgridAxis, dict[str, int | float | np.ndarray]],
395	    vectorfield: VectorField,
396	    a: np.float32,
397	    b: np.float32,
398	):
399	    """Helper function for spatial boundary condition interpolation for velocity fields."""
400	    xi, xsi = grid_positions["X"]["index"], grid_positions["X"]["bcoord"]
401	    yi, eta = grid_positions["Y"]["index"], grid_positions["Y"]["bcoord"]
402	    zi, zeta = grid_positions["Z"]["index"], grid_positions["Z"]["bcoord"]
403	    ti, tau = grid_positions["T"]["index"], grid_positions["T"]["bcoord"]
404	
405	    axis_dim = vectorfield.U.grid.get_axis_dim_mapping(vectorfield.U.data.dims)
406	    lenT = 2 if np.any(tau > 0) else 1
407	    lenZ = 2 if np.any(zeta > 0) else 1
408	    npart = len(xsi)
409	
410	    u = XLinear(particle_positions, grid_positions, vectorfield.U)
411	    v = XLinear(particle_positions, grid_positions, vectorfield.V)
412	    if vectorfield.W:
413	        w = XLinear(particle_positions, grid_positions, vectorfield.W)
414	
415	    corner_dataU = _get_corner_data_Agrid(vectorfield.U.data, ti, zi, yi, xi, lenT, lenZ, npart, axis_dim)
416	    corner_dataV = _get_corner_data_Agrid(vectorfield.V.data, ti, zi, yi, xi, lenT, lenZ, npart, axis_dim)
417	
418	    def is_land(ti: int, zi: int, yi: int, xi: int):
419	        uval = corner_dataU[ti, zi, yi, xi, :]
420	        vval = corner_dataV[ti, zi, yi, xi, :]
421	        return np.where(np.isclose(uval, 0.0) & np.isclose(vval, 0.0), True, False)
422	
423	    f_u = np.ones_like(xsi)
424	    f_v = np.ones_like(eta)
425	
426	    if lenZ == 1:
427	        f_u = np.where(is_land(0, 0, 0, 0) & is_land(0, 0, 0, 1) & (eta > 0), f_u * (a + b * eta) / eta, f_u)
428	        f_u = np.where(is_land(0, 0, 1, 0) & is_land(0, 0, 1, 1) & (eta < 1), f_u * (1 - b * eta) / (1 - eta), f_u)
429	        f_v = np.where(is_land(0, 0, 0, 0) & is_land(0, 0, 1, 0) & (xsi > 0), f_v * (a + b * xsi) / xsi, f_v)
430	        f_v = np.where(is_land(0, 0, 0, 1) & is_land(0, 0, 1, 1) & (xsi < 1), f_v * (1 - b * xsi) / (1 - xsi), f_v)
431	    else:
432	        f_u = np.where(
433	            is_land(0, 0, 0, 0) & is_land(0, 0, 0, 1) & is_land(0, 1, 0, 0) & is_land(0, 1, 0, 1) & (eta > 0),
434	            f_u * (a + b * eta) / eta,
435	            f_u,
436	        )
437	        f_u = np.where(
438	            is_land(0, 0, 1, 0) & is_land(0, 0, 1, 1) & is_land(0, 1, 1, 0) & is_land(0, 1, 1, 1) & (eta < 1),
439	            f_u * (1 - b * eta) / (1 - eta),
440	            f_u,
441	        )
442	        f_v = np.where(
443	            is_land(0, 0, 0, 0) & is_land(0, 0, 1, 0) & is_land(0, 1, 0, 0) & is_land(0, 1, 1, 0) & (xsi > 0),
444	            f_v * (a + b * xsi) / xsi,
445	            f_v,
446	        )
447	        f_v = np.where(
448	            is_land(0, 0, 0, 1) & is_land(0, 0, 1, 1) & is_land(0, 1, 0, 1) & is_land(0, 1, 1, 1) & (xsi < 1),
449	            f_v * (1 - b * xsi) / (1 - xsi),
450	            f_v,
451	        )
452	        f_u = np.where(
453	            is_land(0, 0, 0, 0) & is_land(0, 0, 0, 1) & is_land(0, 0, 1, 0 & is_land(0, 0, 1, 1) & (zeta > 0)),
454	            f_u * (a + b * zeta) / zeta,
455	            f_u,
456	        )
457	        f_u = np.where(
458	            is_land(0, 1, 0, 0) & is_land(0, 1, 0, 1) & is_land(0, 1, 1, 0 & is_land(0, 1, 1, 1) & (zeta < 1)),
459	            f_u * (1 - b * zeta) / (1 - zeta),
460	            f_u,
461	        )
462	        f_v = np.where(
463	            is_land(0, 0, 0, 0) & is_land(0, 0, 0, 1) & is_land(0, 0, 1, 0 & is_land(0, 0, 1, 1) & (zeta > 0)),
464	            f_v * (a + b * zeta) / zeta,
465	            f_v,
466	        )
467	        f_v = np.where(
468	            is_land(0, 1, 0, 0) & is_land(0, 1, 0, 1) & is_land(0, 1, 1, 0 & is_land(0, 1, 1, 1) & (zeta < 1)),
469	            f_v * (1 - b * zeta) / (1 - zeta),
470	            f_v,

478	            is_land(0, 0, 0, 0) & is_land(0, 0, 0, 1) & is_land(0, 1, 0, 0) & is_land(0, 1, 0, 1) & (eta > 0),
479	            f_w * (a + b * eta) / eta,

483	            is_land(0, 0, 1, 0) & is_land(0, 0, 1, 1) & is_land(0, 1, 1, 0) & is_land(0, 1, 1, 1) & (eta < 1),
484	            f_w * (a - b * eta) / (1 - eta),
485	            f_w,

487	        f_w = np.where(
488	            is_land(0, 0, 0, 0) & is_land(0, 0, 1, 0) & is_land(0, 1, 0, 0) & is_land(0, 1, 1, 0) & (xsi > 0),

522	def XNearest(
523	    particle_positions: dict[str, float | np.ndarray],
524	    grid_positions: dict[XgridAxis, dict[str, int | float | np.ndarray]],
525	    field: Field,
526	):
527	    """
528	    Nearest-Neighbour spatial interpolation on a regular grid.
529	    Note that this still uses linear interpolation in time.
530	    """
531	    xi, xsi = grid_positions["X"]["index"], grid_positions["X"]["bcoord"]
532	    yi, eta = grid_positions["Y"]["index"], grid_positions["Y"]["bcoord"]
533	    zi, zeta = grid_positions["Z"]["index"], grid_positions["Z"]["bcoord"]
534	    ti, tau = grid_positions["T"]["index"], grid_positions["T"]["bcoord"]
535	
536	    axis_dim = field.grid.get_axis_dim_mapping(field.data.dims)
537	    data = field.data
538	
539	    lenT = 2 if np.any(tau > 0) else 1
540	
541	    # Spatial coordinates: left if barycentric < 0.5, otherwise right
542	    zi_1 = np.clip(zi + 1, 0, data.shape[1] - 1)
543	    zi_full = np.where(zeta < 0.5, zi, zi_1)
544	
545	    yi_1 = np.clip(yi + 1, 0, data.shape[2] - 1)
546	    yi_full = np.where(eta < 0.5, yi, yi_1)
547	
548	    xi_1 = np.clip(xi + 1, 0, data.shape[3] - 1)
549	    xi_full = np.where(xsi < 0.5, xi, xi_1)
550	
551	    # Time coordinates: 1 point at ti, then 1 point at ti+1
552	    if lenT == 1:
553	        ti_full = ti
554	    else:
555	        ti_1 = np.clip(ti + 1, 0, data.shape[0] - 1)
556	        ti_full = np.concatenate([ti, ti_1])
557	        xi_full = np.repeat(xi_full, 2)
558	        yi_full = np.repeat(yi_full, 2)
559	        zi_full = np.repeat(zi_full, 2)
560	
561	    # Create DataArrays for indexing
562	    selection_dict = {
563	        axis_dim["X"]: xr.DataArray(xi_full, dims=("points")),
564	        axis_dim["Y"]: xr.DataArray(yi_full, dims=("points")),
565	    }
566	    if "Z" in axis_dim:
567	        selection_dict[axis_dim["Z"]] = xr.DataArray(zi_full, dims=("points"))
568	    if "time" in data.dims:
569	        selection_dict["time"] = xr.DataArray(ti_full, dims=("points"))
570	
571	    corner_data = data.isel(selection_dict).data.reshape(lenT, len(xsi))
572	
573	    if lenT == 2:
574	        value = corner_data[0, :] * (1 - tau) + corner_data[1, :] * tau
575	    else:
576	        value = corner_data[0, :]
577	
578	    return value.compute() if is_dask_collection(value) else value

581	def XLinearInvdistLandTracer(
582	    particle_positions: dict[str, float | np.ndarray],
583	    grid_positions: dict[XgridAxis, dict[str, int | float | np.ndarray]],
584	    field: Field,
585	):
586	    """Linear spatial interpolation on a regular grid, where points on land are not used."""
587	    values = XLinear(particle_positions, grid_positions, field)
588	
589	    xi, xsi = grid_positions["X"]["index"], grid_positions["X"]["bcoord"]
590	    yi, eta = grid_positions["Y"]["index"], grid_positions["Y"]["bcoord"]
591	    zi, zeta = grid_positions["Z"]["index"], grid_positions["Z"]["bcoord"]
592	    ti, tau = grid_positions["T"]["index"], grid_positions["T"]["bcoord"]
593	
594	    axis_dim = field.grid.get_axis_dim_mapping(field.data.dims)
595	    lenT = 2 if np.any(tau > 0) else 1
596	    lenZ = 2 if np.any(zeta > 0) else 1
597	
598	    corner_data = _get_corner_data_Agrid(field.data, ti, zi, yi, xi, lenT, lenZ, len(xsi), axis_dim)
599	
600	    land_mask = np.isclose(corner_data, 0.0)
601	    nb_land = np.sum(land_mask, axis=(0, 1, 2, 3))
602	
603	    if np.any(nb_land):
604	        all_land_mask = nb_land == 4 * lenZ * lenT
605	        values[all_land_mask] = 0.0
606	
607	        some_land = np.logical_and(nb_land > 0, nb_land < 4 * lenZ * lenT)
608	        if np.any(some_land):
609	            i_grid = np.arange(2)[None, None, None, :, None]
610	            j_grid = np.arange(2)[None, None, :, None, None]
611	            eta_b = eta[None, None, None, None, :]
612	            xsi_b = xsi[None, None, None, None, :]
613	
614	            dist2 = (eta_b - j_grid) ** 2 + (xsi_b - i_grid) ** 2
615	
616	            valid_mask = ~land_mask
617	            # Normal inverse-distance weighting
618	            inv_dist = 1.0 / dist2
619	            weighted = np.where(valid_mask, corner_data * inv_dist, 0.0)
620	
621	            val = np.sum(weighted, axis=(0, 1, 2, 3))
622	            w_sum = np.sum(np.where(valid_mask, inv_dist, 0.0), axis=(0, 1, 2, 3))
623	
624	            values[some_land] = val[some_land] / w_sum[some_land]
625	
626	            # If a particle hits exactly one of the 8 corner points, extract it
627	            exact_mask = dist2 == 0 & valid_mask
628	            exact_vals = np.sum(np.where(exact_mask, corner_data, 0.0), axis=(0, 1, 2, 3))
629	            has_exact = np.any(exact_mask, axis=(0, 1, 2, 3))
630	
631	            exact_particles = some_land & has_exact
632	            values[exact_particles] = exact_vals[exact_particles]
633	
634	    return values.compute() if is_dask_collection(values) else values

48	class Field:
49	    """The Field class that holds scalar field data.
50	    The `Field` object is a wrapper around a xarray.DataArray or uxarray.UxDataArray object.
51	    Additionally, it holds a dynamic Callable procedure that is used to interpolate the field data.
52	    During initialization, the user is required to supply a custom interpolation method that is used
53	    to interpolate the field data, so long as the interpolation method has the correct signature.
54	
55	    Notes
56	    -----
57	    The xarray.DataArray or uxarray.UxDataArray object contains the field data and metadata.
58	
59	    * dims: (time, [nz1 | nz], [face_lat | node_lat | edge_lat], [face_lon | node_lon | edge_lon])
60	    * attrs: (location, mesh, mesh)
61	
62	    When using a xarray.DataArray object:
63	
64	    * The xarray.DataArray object must have the "location" and "mesh" attributes set.
65	    * The "location" attribute must be set to one of the following to define which pairing of points a field is associated with:
66	        * "node"
67	        * "face"
68	        * "x_edge"
69	        * "y_edge"
70	
71	    * For an A-Grid, the "location" attribute must be set to / is assumed to be "node" (node_lat,node_lon).
72	    * For a C-Grid, the "location" setting for a field has the following interpretation:
73	        * "node" ~> the field is associated with the vorticity points (node_lat, node_lon)
74	        * "face" ~> the field is associated with the tracer points (face_lat, face_lon)
75	        * "x_edge" ~> the field is associated with the u-velocity points (face_lat, node_lon)
76	        * "y_edge" ~> the field is associated with the v-velocity points (node_lat, face_lon)
77	
78	    When using a uxarray.UxDataArray object:
79	
80	    * The uxarray.UxDataArray.UxGrid object must have the "Conventions" attribute set to "UGRID-1.0"
81	      and the uxarray.UxDataArray object must comply with the UGRID conventions.
82	      See https://ugrid-conventions.github.io/ugrid-conventions/ for more information.
83	
84	    """
85	
86	    def __init__(
87	        self,
88	        name: str,
89	        data: xr.DataArray | ux.UxDataArray,
90	        grid: UxGrid | XGrid,
91	        interp_method: Callable,
92	    ):
93	        if not isinstance(data, (ux.UxDataArray, xr.DataArray)):
94	            raise ValueError(
95	                f"Expected `data` to be a uxarray.UxDataArray or xarray.DataArray object, got {type(data)}."
96	            )
97	
98	        _assert_str_and_python_varname(name)
99	
100	        if not isinstance(grid, (UxGrid, XGrid)):
101	            raise ValueError(f"Expected `grid` to be a parcels UxGrid, or parcels XGrid object, got {type(grid)}.")
102	
103	        _assert_compatible_combination(data, grid)
104	
105	        if isinstance(grid, XGrid):
106	            assert_all_field_dims_have_axis(data, grid.xgcm_grid)
107	            data = _transpose_xfield_data_to_tzyx(data, grid.xgcm_grid)
108	
109	        self.name = name
110	        self.data = data
111	        self.grid = grid
112	
113	        try:
114	            self.time_interval = _get_time_interval(data)
115	        except ValueError as e:
116	            e.add_note(
117	                f"Error getting time interval for field {name!r}. Are you sure that the time dimension on the xarray dataset is stored as timedelta, datetime or cftime datetime objects?"
118	            )
119	            raise e
120	
121	        try:
122	            if isinstance(data, ux.UxDataArray):
123	                _assert_valid_uxdataarray(data)
124	                # TODO: For unstructured grids, validate that `data.uxgrid` is the same as `grid`
125	            else:
126	                pass  # TODO v4: Add validation for xr.DataArray objects
127	        except Exception as e:
128	            e.add_note(f"Error validating field {name!r}.")
129	            raise e
130	
131	        # Setting the interpolation method dynamically
132	        assert_same_function_signature(interp_method, ref=ZeroInterpolator, context="Interpolation")
133	        self._interp_method = interp_method
134	
135	        self.igrid = -1  # Default the grid index to -1
136	
137	        if self.data.shape[0] > 1:
138	            if "time" not in self.data.coords:
139	                raise ValueError("Field data is missing a 'time' coordinate.")

187	    def eval(self, time: datetime, z, y, x, particles=None):
188	        """Interpolate field values in space and time.
189	
190	        Parameters
191	        ----------
192	        time : float or array-like
193	            Time(s) at which to sample the field.
194	        z, y, x : scalar or array-like
195	            Vertical (z), latitudinal (y) and longitudinal (x) positions to sample.
196	            Inputs are promoted to 1-D arrays internally.
197	        particles : ParticleSet, optional
198	            If provided, used to associate results with particle indices and to

210	          interpolation values.
211	        """

213	            _ei = None
214	        else:

217	        y = np.atleast_1d(y)
218	        x = np.atleast_1d(x)
219	
220	        particle_positions, grid_positions = _get_positions(self, time, z, y, x, particles, _ei)

215	def _unravel(dims, ei):
216	    """
217	    Converts a flattened (raveled) index back to multi-dimensional indices.
218	
219	    Args:
220	        dims (1d-array-like): The dimensions along each axis
221	        ei (int): The flattened index to convert
222	
223	    Returns
224	    -------
225	        array-like: Indices along each axis corresponding to the given flattened index
226	
227	    Example:
228	        >>> dims = [2, 3, 4]
229	        >>> ei = 9
230	        >>> unravel(dims, ei)
231	        array([0, 2, 1])
232	        # Calculation:
233	        # i0 = 9 // (3*4) = 9 // 12 = 0
234	        # remainder = 9 % 12 = 9
235	        # i1 = 9 // 4 = 2
236	        # i2 = 9 % 4 = 1
237	    """
238	    strides = np.cumprod(dims[::-1])[::-1]
239	
240	    indices = np.empty((len(dims), len(ei)), dtype=int)
241	
242	    for i in range(len(dims) - 1):
243	        indices[i, :] = ei // strides[i + 1]
244	        ei = ei % strides[i + 1]
245	
246	    indices[-1, :] = ei
247	    return indices
248	
249	
250	def _ravel(dims, indices):
251	    """
252	    Converts indices to a flattened (raveled) index.
253	
254	    Args:
255	        dims (1d-array-like): The dimensions along each axis
256	        indices (array-like): Indices along each axis to convert
257	
258	    Returns
259	    -------
260	        int: The flattened index corresponding to the given indices
261	
262	    Example:
263	        >>> dims = [2, 3, 4]
264	        >>> indices = [0, 2, 1]
265	        >>> ravel(dims, indices)
266	        9
267	        # Calculation: 0 * (3 * 4) + 2 * (4) + 1 = 0 + 8 + 1 = 9
268	    """
269	    strides = np.cumprod(dims[::-1])[::-1]
270	    ei = 0
271	    for i in range(len(dims) - 1):
272	        ei += indices[i] * strides[i + 1]
273	
274	    return ei + indices[-1]

import math

import numpy as np
import xarray as xr

from parcels._core.utils.sgrid import (
    FaceNodePadding,
    Grid2DMetadata,
    Padding,
    _attach_sgrid_metadata,
)
from parcels._core.utils.time import timedelta_to_float


def simple_UV_dataset(dims=(360, 2, 30, 4), maxdepth=1, mesh="spherical"):
    max_lon = 180.0 if mesh == "spherical" else 1e6
    max_lat = 90.0 if mesh == "spherical" else 1e6

    return xr.Dataset(
        {"U": (["time", "depth", "YG", "XG"], np.zeros(dims)), "V": (["time", "depth", "YG", "XG"], np.zeros(dims))},
        coords={
            "time": (["time"], xr.date_range("2000", "2001", dims[0]), {"axis": "T"}),
            "depth": (["depth"], np.linspace(0, maxdepth, dims[1]), {"axis": "Z"}),
            "YC": (["YC"], np.arange(dims[2]) + 0.5, {"axis": "Y"}),
            "YG": (["YG"], np.arange(dims[2]), {"axis": "Y", "c_grid_axis_shift": -0.5}),
            "XC": (["XC"], np.arange(dims[3]) + 0.5, {"axis": "X"}),
            "XG": (["XG"], np.arange(dims[3]), {"axis": "X", "c_grid_axis_shift": -0.5}),
            "lat": (["YG"], np.linspace(-max_lat, max_lat, dims[2]), {"axis": "Y", "c_grid_axis_shift": -0.5}),
            "lon": (["XG"], np.linspace(-max_lon, max_lon, dims[3]), {"axis": "X", "c_grid_axis_shift": -0.5}),
        },
    ).pipe(
        _attach_sgrid_metadata,
        Grid2DMetadata(
            cf_role="grid_topology",
            topology_dimension=2,
            node_dimensions=("XG", "YG"),
            face_dimensions=(
                FaceNodePadding("XC", "XG", Padding.LOW),
                FaceNodePadding("YC", "YG", Padding.LOW),
            ),
            vertical_dimensions=(FaceNodePadding("ZC", "depth", Padding.BOTH),),
        ),
    )


def radial_rotation_dataset(xdim=200, ydim=200):  # Define 2D flat, square fieldset for testing purposes.
    lon = np.linspace(0, 60, xdim, dtype=np.float32)
    lat = np.linspace(0, 60, ydim, dtype=np.float32)

    x0 = 30.0  # Define the origin to be the centre of the Field.
    y0 = 30.0

    U = np.zeros((2, 1, ydim, xdim), dtype=np.float32)
    V = np.zeros((2, 1, ydim, xdim), dtype=np.float32)

    omega = 2 * np.pi / 86400.0  # Define the rotational period as 1 day.

    for i in range(lon.size):
        for j in range(lat.size):
            r = np.sqrt((lon[i] - x0) ** 2 + (lat[j] - y0) ** 2)
            assert r >= 0.0
            assert r <= np.sqrt(x0**2 + y0**2)

            theta = np.arctan2((lat[j] - y0), (lon[i] - x0))
            assert abs(theta) <= np.pi

            U[:, :, j, i] = r * np.sin(theta) * omega
            V[:, :, j, i] = -r * np.cos(theta) * omega

    return xr.Dataset(
        {"U": (["time", "depth", "YG", "XG"], U), "V": (["time", "depth", "YG", "XG"], V)},
        coords={
            "time": (["time"], [np.timedelta64(0, "s"), np.timedelta64(10, "D")], {"axis": "T"}),
            "depth": (["depth"], np.array([0.0]), {"axis": "Z"}),
            "YC": (["YC"], np.arange(ydim) + 0.5, {"axis": "Y"}),
            "YG": (["YG"], np.arange(ydim), {"axis": "Y", "c_grid_axis_shift": -0.5}),
            "XC": (["XC"], np.arange(xdim) + 0.5, {"axis": "X"}),
            "XG": (["XG"], np.arange(xdim), {"axis": "X", "c_grid_axis_shift": -0.5}),
            "lat": (["YG"], lat, {"axis": "Y", "c_grid_axis_shift": 0.5}),
            "lon": (["XG"], lon, {"axis": "X", "c_grid_axis_shift": -0.5}),
        },
    )


def moving_eddy_dataset(xdim=2, ydim=2):  # TODO check if this also works with xdim=1, ydim=1
    """Create a dataset with an eddy moving in time. Note that there is no spatial variation in the flow."""
    f, u_0, u_g = 1.0e-4, 0.3, 0.04  # Some constants

    lon = np.linspace(0, 25000, xdim, dtype=np.float32)
    lat = np.linspace(0, 25000, ydim, dtype=np.float32)

    time = np.arange(np.timedelta64(0, "s"), np.timedelta64(7, "h"), np.timedelta64(1, "m"))

    U = np.zeros((len(time), 1, ydim, xdim), dtype=np.float32)
    V = np.zeros((len(time), 1, ydim, xdim), dtype=np.float32)

    for t in range(len(time)):
        U[t, :, :, :] = u_g + (u_0 - u_g) * np.cos(f * timedelta_to_float(time[t]))
        V[t, :, :, :] = -(u_0 - u_g) * np.sin(f * timedelta_to_float(time[t]))

    return xr.Dataset(
        {"U": (["time", "depth", "YG", "XG"], U), "V": (["time", "depth", "YG", "XG"], V)},
        coords={
            "time": (["time"], time, {"axis": "T"}),
            "depth": (["depth"], np.array([0.0]), {"axis": "Z"}),
            "YC": (["YC"], np.arange(ydim) + 0.5, {"axis": "Y"}),
            "YG": (["YG"], np.arange(ydim), {"axis": "Y", "c_grid_axis_shift": -0.5}),
            "XC": (["XC"], np.arange(xdim) + 0.5, {"axis": "X"}),
            "XG": (["XG"], np.arange(xdim), {"axis": "X", "c_grid_axis_shift": -0.5}),
            "lat": (["YG"], lat, {"axis": "Y", "c_grid_axis_shift": 0.5}),
            "lon": (["XG"], lon, {"axis": "X", "c_grid_axis_shift": -0.5}),
        },
        attrs={
            "u_0": u_0,
            "u_g": u_g,
            "f": f,
        },
    )
